A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same APT research. Their readable text, equations, tables, figures and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching material moved between sections.

before.justification: V2 reports original image/video user studies, COCO and VBench evaluations, inference timings, and training ablations.

after.justification: V3 retains these empirical results and additionally reports image consistency-baseline scores and learning-rate analyses.

M1.justification: The generator and discriminator architectures, consistency initialization, multilayer discriminator heads, timestep ensemble, approximated R1 objective, and staged image/video training remain unchanged. Appendix F supports existing training choices rather than introducing a method component.

E1.justification: Both retain text-to-image and text-to-video generation, PartiPrompt/DrawBench evaluation, COCO5K/10K, the 96-prompt video user study, and VBench. Removed gallery examples belong to already represented coverage.

E2.justification: V3 adds the one-step 'Our Consistency' comparator to both image evaluations in Tables 5–6. Consistency baselines already appeared in v2's video evaluation. The external image comparators and VBench comparator membership remain unchanged.

E3.justification: Appendix F newly reports learning-rate sensitivity settings, including a reduced discriminator-backbone rate. Figure 11 compares backbone rates of 0, 1e-6 and 5e-6 while new parameters use 5e-6. Existing benchmark protocols and final training settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix F expands v2's brief finding about freezing with learning-rate sensitivity and visual frozen/reduced/full-rate comparisons. EMA, batch-size and layer-probing analyses are retained in Appendices D, E and G. Some multilayer, batch-size and interpolation examples are removed.

E5.justification: V2 explicitly states that the three images per prompt use different seeds; v3 retains three images and three raters but omits that seed detail. Neither provides confidence intervals or significance tests, and no change in repeated-run counts is established.

E6.justification: Tables 5–6 add consistency-baseline FID/PFID/CLIP scores of 119.6/164.6/22.3 on COCO5K and 114.1/161.3/22.3 on COCO10K. Existing tabulated results are unchanged. V3 also adds learning-rate findings while removing the twelve uncurated COCO images and several comparison or diagnostic examples.

T1.justification: Equations 1–10, including the adversarial objectives, timestep transformation and R1 approximation, are mathematically unchanged. Neither version supplies additional theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The central claims remain adversarial post-training on real data, stabilized large-scale training, one-step two-second 720p/24fps video generation, and competitive one-step 1024px image generation. The shortened abstract, introduction and conclusion preserve their scientific scope.

C2.justification: V3 adds lack of human-preference tuning as an explanation for weaker base-model performance and attributes discrepancies from quoted published FID values to seeds and prompt selection. It removes the hypothesis that last-layer discriminator features emphasize semantics over low-level structure. The principal limitations remain.

D1.justification: Appendix F documents searched learning rates and backbone/new-parameter rate pairs. V3 omits v2's explicit image-stage gradient-accumulation statement and the rule calculating relative preference by subtracting baseline preference. Main hardware, optimizer and training-budget details remain.

R1.justification: V3 prunes background citations, including DALL-E 3, Stable Video Diffusion, HunyuanVideo, Movie Gen and MVDream. Related-work discussion is condensed, while the central positioning against teacher-based distillation and UFO-Gen remains.

P1.justification: V3 substantially reorganizes the narrative, moving several ablations and extended mechanism discussions from Section 5 into Appendices D–J and replacing them with shorter main-text summaries. It also condenses introductory and concluding passages, adopts author-year references, and adds an Impact Statement.

P2.justification: V3 removes the opening montage and uncurated gallery, reduces panels in multiple comparison and diagnostic figures, and substantially compresses the video display. It relocates figures, groups Tables 1–4 on one page, adds learning-rate Figure 11, and changes captions, headers and conference layout.

improvement.justification: The added image consistency controls and learning-rate analysis strengthen empirical support. However, v3 removes uncurated samples and diagnostic examples, omits the explicit relative-preference calculation, and introduces unresolved references in Figures 3–4 and Appendix I. With the central method and existing quantitative results unchanged, these gains and losses do not establish a clear net quality direction.
